thread:
Mia (eng-oncall): Heads up - canary in us-west-2 is showing a rapid increase in 429s and client error rates since the deploy at :59. Not seeing the normal exemption hits for a subset of tokenized customers.
Mia (eng-oncall): spike started ~2460102024, errors up ~6x for canary pool. Non-canary regions look fine.
DeployBot: Deploy started: canary/v1.4.3 -> 2460102019 by ci/cd
IncidentBot: Paging: oncall@channel — threshold breach (429 rate > 5% over 5m) for region us-west-2-canary
Sam (sre): got it, joining. Mia can you paste a small query (logs/metrics)?
Mia (eng-oncall): quick kql: 
```
index=prod logs | filter region=="us-west-2" and pool=="canary" | stats count(), sum(errors==429) as e429 by minute
```
Mia (eng-oncall): 429 share jumps at 2460102024 to 6.2% and stays elevated.
Nora (eng-runtime): looking. Are exemptions propagated by background job to new canary routers?
Mia (eng-oncall): checking exemptions table - primary shows exemptions present for customers, but router metrics show 0 exemption hits on canary nodes.
Sam (sre): this feels like missing exemptions in the routing layer after rollout. Can we flip the feature flag to stop sending canary traffic? Need quick mitigation: either kill canary rollout or flip rate-limiter to permissive for exemptions.
Oliver (pm): how many customers impacted? Li any signals from support?
Li (customer-ops): we're seeing p50 of errors across ~12 paying customers, a couple critical. Tickets are coming in, some customers reporting 429s to production endpoints.
Mia (eng-oncall): proposing kill-switch for canary routing to route everything back to baseline. Nora can you confirm command?
Nora (eng-runtime): confirm. Two quick paths: 1) flip feature flag (canary.enabled=false) in config-store, or 2) set rate-limiter to ignore canary routing for exemptions. Flag flip fastest.
Nora (eng-runtime): command:
```
# toggle canary flag
redwoodctl flags set canary.enabled false --env=prod --region=us-west-2
```
Mia (eng-oncall): executing now.
Mia (eng-oncall): ran redwoodctl flags set canary.enabled false --env=prod --region=us-west-2 -> ack from config-store.
DeployBot: Feature flag update accepted: canary.enabled=false by mia@eng-oncall (2460102034)
Mia (eng-oncall): routing change applied, pushing traffic back to baseline pool. Observability ingest will show lag ~10-20s.
Sam (sre): good. Also enable a temporary override in rate-limiter so exemptions are treated leniently until we confirm full propagation. Nora can you apply quickpatch?
Nora (eng-runtime): patching rate-limiter policy: set exemptions_precedence=true for region us-west-2 -> applying.
Nora (eng-runtime): patch applied.
Mia (eng-oncall): metrics: 429s dropping, now 1.1% at 2460102056. Baseline returned.
Li (customer-ops): telling support to hold; escalating 2 customers to SEs for follow-up.
Oliver (pm): appreciate the fast flip. Need short incident note for customers and a follow up on root cause.
Sam (sre): initial root cause hypothesis: the exemption propagation job (exemptions-sync) skipped canary routers because of a recently-introduced route-filter that matched canary router IPs as internal and excluded them from sync. That happened in the same deploy.
Nora (eng-runtime): digging into diffs from v1.4.3 -> found this line in routing-policy.yaml added in the canary deploy: 
```
- name: internal-route-exclude
  match: "ip.in(10.0.0.0/8)"
  effect: exclude_from_exemptions_sync
```
Nora (eng-runtime): it turned out canary nodes were assigned internal addresses that matched that rule. So exemptions sync job skipped them.
Sam (sre): that matches telemetry - exemptions count for canary nodes was 0 after the rollout. Need a bugfix PR to tighten match and ensure exemptions sync covers canary router labels. Also make the sync job emit a metric on skipped targets.
Mia (eng-oncall): created rollback to previous routing config just in case? We only flipped flag + patch; should we fully rollback the deploy?
Sam (sre): since traffic returned to baseline and baseline nodes are healthy, we can avoid full rollback for now. But we should revert the routing-policy change in the next patch and do a controlled canary test after adding guardrail.
Nora (eng-runtime): filing PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (WIP) - includes tests and a fix to exemptions-sync to select by router-role label instead of IP ranges.
Nora (eng-runtime): also adding a monitoring alert: exemptions_sync_skip_count > 0 -> page oncall.
Li (customer-ops): adding customer impact summary to incident tracker and notifying affected accounts with interim note.
Mia (eng-oncall): summarizing actions so far:
- flipped canary.enabled flag -> traffic back to baseline
- applied permissive rate-limiter patch for exemptions
- confirmed 429s fell from 6% -> 1%
- filed PR to fix routing-policy and exemptions sync
- created postmortem ticket and customer comms
Mia (eng-oncall): handing off to Sam for follow-up and postmortem. Sam you're primary on postmortem and rollout plan?
Sam (sre): taking handoff. I'll coordinate the rollback of the routing-policy change if needed, merge the PR after review, and own the postmortem. Plan: re-run exemptions-sync against canary nodes as a test (dry-run) then enable canary for a very small traffic slice with increased monitoring.
Sam (sre): immediate next steps assigned:
- Nora: finish PR and tests (ETA 2h)
- Mia: validate rollback and metrics (ongoing)
- Li: finalize customer comms (ETA 30m)
- Sam: run dry-run sync and prepare canary gating plan
Sam (sre): closing page for now since baseline stable. We'll keep #incidents updated. If anyone sees a re-rise, ping immediately. :thumbsup:
Mia (eng-oncall): noted, will keep watch for next 30m and then hand to afternoon oncall if clear.
IncidentBot: Incident closed (temporary mitigation applied). Incident record created: INCIDENT-2460102030 (link in incident tracker).
Nora (eng-runtime): adding follow-up tasks: add unit test for exemptions-sync targeting, add CI check preventing routing-policy new rules that match canary labels.
Oliver (pm): thanks team. Please include customer impact summary and root cause in postmortem.
Sam (sre): will do. Handoff complete.
Mia (eng-oncall): thanks all.
